newsitem.title: CHINA: China consumption, value-added tax behind target.
newsitem.headline: China consumption, value-added tax behind target.

text.p: China's collection of consumption taxes and value-added taxes in January-August was behind target with just 61.7 percent of the annual goal met, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
Consumption taxes and value-added taxes totalled 225.6 billion yuan in January to August of 1996, up 17.7 percent compared with the same period a year ago, the newspaper said.
The figure was just 61.7 percent of the annual target although 66.7 percent of the year had passed, it said.
"The situation is not optimistic," it said.
Export tax rebates were 53.5 billion yuan in the first eight months of the year, up 27.8 percent compared with the same period a year ago and meeting 82.3 percent of the annual target, it said.
Industrial and commercial taxes in the first eight months were 402.3 billion yuan, a rise of 21.4 percent compared with the year ago period, it said.
That figure had met 66.8 percent of the target for all of 1996, it said It gave no further details.
Tax authorities have said serious flooding across much of China in July and August had hampered tax collection.
